title: Using Deterrence to Tackle Second-hand Smoke in Homes
what_it_is: Using Deterrence to Tackle Second-hand Smoke in Homes

sections.label: Second-hand smoke deaths in Singapore
sections.summary: About one person in Singapore dies daily from second-hand smoke, based on 383 deaths in 2016, a number growing yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: About one person in Singapore dies every day due to second-hand smoke.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This is based on the 383 deaths in 2016 and the number of deaths has been growing each year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This is about five times the number of people who have died in motor accidents; seven times the number of people who have died from the coronavirus; and 12 times the number of people who have died from workplace injuries.

sections.label: Second-hand smoke harms children
sections.summary: A recent study concluded children exposed to second-hand smoke from pregnancy to childhood were more likely to suffer ADHD symptoms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In a recent study published just a few months ago, researchers concluded that children exposed to second-hand smoke from pregnancy to childhood were more likely to suffer from ADHD symptoms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Second-hand smoke causes severe respiratory infections, triggers more frequent and more severe asthma attacks, cough, wheezing, breathlessness, ear infections and a whole slew of other illnesses among young children.

sections.label: Environmental Public Health Act nuisances
sections.summary: Section 43 empowers NEA to remove public nuisances, which section 44 defines to include fumes, vapours, gases, heat, radiation or smells.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Section 43 of the Environmental Public Health Act empowers NEA to take any step necessary to remove nuisances of a public nature.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: These nuisances, as defined in section 44, include “the issue of any fumes, vapours, gases, heat, radiation or smells in any premises which is a nuisance or injurious or dangerous to health.” That sure sounds like second-hand smoke.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Why is the Government not using this law to take a clear stance that smoking near windows and at balconies is illegal?

sections.label: Penalties for nuisance orders
sections.summary: Penalties for not complying with nuisance orders under the Environmental Public Health Act are a $10,000 fine, or up to $20,000 or three months' imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Used in conjunction with a law, however, such low-effort enforcement may be sufficient to end bad behaviour in most cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I have no doubt that the majority of people will comply once they realise that the penalty for not complying with nuisance orders under the Environmental Public Health Act is a fine of $10,000 for first-time offenders and in the second or subsequent conviction, to a fine not exceeding $20,000 or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding three months, or to both.

sections.label: Surveillance cameras and privacy
sections.summary: Privacy concerns about surveillance cameras can be minimised by pointing them at the facade of the building, as is already done.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For the small number of cases where we need to deploy a surveillance camera, we can minimise concerns of privacy by doing what we already do: point it at the facade of the building.

sections.label: Project Balefire smoking detection
sections.summary: NEA has collaborated with GovTech on Project Balefire, which aims to detect smoking activities using video analytics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: NEA has collaborated with GovTech on Project Balefire, which aims to detect smoking activities using video analytics.

sections.label: Second-hand smoke at home
sections.summary: Section 43 of the Environmental Public Health Act can penalise smoking near windows and balconies, and deterrence is key, as many are exposed to second-hand smoke at home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Section 43 of the Environmental Public Health Act can already be used to penalise smoking near windows and at balconies and deterrence rather than enforcement is the key.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This has meant keeping them at home for work and for studies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But this also meant many more are now exposed to the silent pandemic of second-hand smoke at home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: People need to feel safe in their homes again.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Let us use it so Singaporeans feel safe in their homes again.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The World Health Organization revealed that annually 1.2 million non-smokers die from exposure to second-hand smoke.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And 65,000 children die from illnesses related to its poisonous and harmful chemicals.

sections.label: No legal right to stop smoking
sections.summary: Town Council, HDB, NEA and Police officers have been called to assist residents, but no one, including the Member of Parliament, has any legal right to stop anyone smoking at their window or balcony.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Town Council, HDB, NEA and even Police officers have been called upon to assist residents in some of these incidents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: However, no one, including myself as their representative Member of Parliament, has any legal right to stop anyone from smoking at their window or balconies.

sections.label: Smoking prevalence rate 10.1%
sections.summary: In the announcement made on 11 July 2021, a smoking prevalence rate of 10.1% was achieved, just slightly shy of the 10% target.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In the recent announcement made on 11 July 2021, we achieved a smoking prevalence rate of 10.1%, just slightly shy of the 10% target.

sections.label: Ban smoking at balconies and windows
sections.summary: The living environment of non-smokers must be addressed, and smoking prohibition has been expanded to more than 32,000 places.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The living environment of non-smokers must be addressed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I am in favour for the call to ban smoking at all balconies and windows.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: As part of our national health policy to discourage smoking and protect the public from second-hand smoke, we have expanded smoking prohibition extensively, to more than 32,000 places.

sections.label: Singapore smoking prevalence 10.1% in 2020
sections.summary: Through concerted efforts, Singapore's smoking prevalence was driven down to 10.1% in 2020, half the global average of 20%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Through concerted efforts, Singapore’s smoking prevalence has been driven down to 10.1% in 2020, half the global average of 20%.

sections.label: Tickets for smoking in prohibited areas
sections.summary: Eleven thousand tickets were issued in 2020 compared to 7,100 in 2019 for smoking in prohibited areas such as common corridors and stairwells of flats.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Eleven thousand tickets were issued in 2020 compared to 7,100 in 2019 for smoking in prohibited areas such as common corridors and stairwells of flats which can lead to second-hand smoke in homes.

sections.label: Norfolk public housing smoking ban
sections.summary: Norfolk, Virginia, banned smoking in public housing rental units in 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Norfolk, Virginia, banned smoking in public housing rental units in 2018.

sections.label: San Francisco multi-unit smoking proposal
sections.summary: Last year, the city and county of San Francisco proposed prohibiting smoking in all multi-unit residences.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Last year, the city and county of San Francisco put forward a proposal to prohibit smoking in all multi-unit residences.

sections.label: DSPs, MSO and MND proposals
sections.summary: MSO has rolled out measures in Mountbatten and Pioneer, will bring them to Bukit Gombak, DSPs were piloted in Clementi, and MND called for proposals on second-hand smoke.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: MSO has rolled this out in Mountbatten and Pioneer and will be bringing it to Bukit Gombak.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: In June, two Designated Smoking Points, or DSPs, with improved designs were set up in Clementi as a community pilot project.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Last Friday, MND called for proposals for innovative solutions on managing second-hand smoke from neighbouring homes.

sections.label: Smoker cooperation and recurring feedback
sections.summary: Most smokers cooperate and less than 10% of feedback received recurs within a year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: In fact, most smokers cooperate and thus far, less than 10% of the feedback we received recur within a year.

sections.label: Enforcement and Norfolk deterrence example
sections.summary: Deterrence requires effective enforcement, and Norfolk, Virginia's legislation improved things briefly before returning to normal because residents knew enforcement was difficult.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: As I have said, deterrence will only be achieved not just with an appropriate law but when there is effective enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: I think it is the case, with all the laws that we enforce, we know that we cannot be everywhere.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: But the fact would be that if the potential offenders know that it is easy to evade the law, that the chance of getting caught is very, very low, then it will not be an effective deterrent.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The example I gave of Norfolk, Virginia, is such an example where they implemented the legislation, there was some improvement within a short period but, after a year, it was back to normal because the residents knew that it was very difficult to enforce the legislation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: You actually do not really want to enforce it if nobody breaks the law.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: But at the end of the day, if you cannot enforce it effectively, then it is not going to be a useful deterrent.
